# Purpose and endpoint

Start from **what reproducible research means**, note where definitions diverge (including qualitative work), then teach everyday **workflows**: durable project folder, documentation, versioning, sharing boundaries, responsible AI use.

Students organise a folder and write documentation for **their own PhD project**, then transfer text into the course Swedish Research Council DMP template. **No hand-in to this teaching team.**

**Working definition ([The Turing Way](https://book.the-turing-way.org/reproducible-research/overview/overview-definitions/)):** work that can be independently recreated from the **same data and the same analysis**. Caveats: fields swap *reproducible* / *replicable*; for much qualitative work the practical aim is *auditability* ([Keele KORSA](https://www.keele.ac.uk/korsa/qualitative/reproducibilityreplication/)). KI does not define the term; it requires documentation and openness so research can be followed, interpreted, and reproduced ([Riktlinjer](https://medarbetare.ki.se/media/99275/download) §§6–7; [documentation guidelines](https://staff.ki.se/research-support/research-data-management/plan-your-research-data-management/guidelines-for-research-documentation-and-data-management)).

**5-year test:** someone returning in five years can understand what was done and which decisions were made. (KI retention is ≥10 years.)

| Block | Time | Day 1 | Day 2 |
|-------|------|-------|-------|
| Morning | 09:00–12:00 | Self-study | Self-study |
| Afternoon | 13:00–16:00 | Hybrid: room **Future** + [Zoom](https://ki-se.zoom.us/j/68142022512) | Zoom only (same link) |

# Learning outcomes

By the end of the two days, the student can:

1. **Explain** the Turing Way definition, note where definitions diverge (including qualitative auditability), and relate that to KI’s research and documentation guidelines.
2. **Structure** a durable project folder and its documentation (README, decision log, naming and versioning) so the project passes the 5-year test.
3. **Track** changes and decisions in a form humans and tools can both read, and justify which versioning approach fits their project.
4. **Draft** SRC DMP answers on **documentation**, **data description**, **data quality**, **storage**, **security**, and **who is responsible**.
5. **Judge** what can be shared, what must stay protected, and how to use KI-supported AI (Copilot-first) responsibly — with disclosure and verification.

# Standing rules (every block)

- **Versioning:** prefer one shared master in **Office Online** on KI Teams/SharePoint, with regular downloads named per KI §6.1. Google Docs fine for shared text. Dated copies + decision log OK. Git allowed if already used; do not teach Git.
- **AI:** prefer Microsoft Copilot; never put personal/patient/sensitive research data in prompts; keep prompt + output; verify and edit; disclose to the team.
- **TBL close:** every application ends with **2–3 team findings on the shared board + whole-group discussion** (not classic simultaneous report). **Full** 5-year rubric only in Day 1 App 1 and Day 2 peer critique.
- **DMP:** after each major activity, paste under the exact SRC questions in the map below. Mark text as *draft* for the course assignment.
- Synthetic / fictional data only in examples.

# Day 2 — Versioning, sharing, and the DMP

## Morning (self-study)

| Step | Students do |
|------|-------------|
| 1 | Read GEP **Keeping Track of Changes** (all); **Data Management** 7; **Collaboration** 2–5. Cue Single Master Online → Office Online + §6.1 naming |
| 2 | KI: [Share data and collaborate](https://staff.ki.se/research-support/research-data-management/collaborate-process-analyse-research-data/share-data-and-collaborate); [open-access policy](https://staff.ki.se/research-support/research-data-management/policy-for-open-access-to-research-data); metadata vs raw; §6.1 naming |
| 3 | Skim SRC questions for data quality, storage, security, who is responsible |
| 4 | Bring Day 1 folder + handwritten notes into the afternoon |

**KI corrections on GEP:** approved storage (not personal cloud/USB); consent/ethics/GDPR before licence talk.

# Session → SRC DMP map

Template: [`Swedish_Research_Council_Template__v5.docx`](../Swedish_Research_Council_Template__v5.docx). Only these six areas.

| When | Area | SRC template question |
|------|------|------------------------|
| Day 1 | Data description | *How will data be collected, created or reused?* |
| Day 1 | Data description | *What types of data… format and amount/volume?* |
| Day 1 | Documentation | *How will the material be documented and described…?* |
| Day 2 | Data quality | *How will data quality be safeguarded and documented…?* |
| Day 2 | Storage | *How is storage and backup… safeguarded during the research process?* |
| Day 2 | Security | *How is data security and controlled access… safeguarded…?* |
| Day 2 | Who is responsible | *Who is responsible for data management… during and after the project?* |

# Scope

**In scope:** definition + limits; folder, documentation, versioning, sharing boundaries, responsible AI; the six DMP areas above.

**Out of scope:** programming, statistics, pipelines, containers; Git beyond a short option (see K8F6106); data collection protocol (assignment component 2); other SRC questions (legal, ethics, accessibility, long-term storage, software, DOI, costs); metascience lecture; shared case vignette; minute-level scripts; new TBL hosting.
